summary: Cancelled multipart resubmit loop causing duplicated token accounting and intermittent 429s on dedicated pool
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports a pattern of intermittent 429 responses from our hosted endpoint when they run a multi-file multipart upload job from their dedicated pool. The uploads were being retried automatically by their client after the initial multipart was cancelled on the client side, and we observe token accounting spikes that correlate with the retries.

Impact: 10-20% of the customer's background imports fail with 429s during the resubmit phase, causing their downstream indexing pipeline to stall for ~5-15 minutes per job. This is affecting production ingestion for several business-critical datasets.

Environment: Dedicated pool (dp-qa-03) backing Datawave org; prod-us-west region; single API key scoped to org-level ingest; affected model embedder-large-v2.

Steps to reproduce (provided by customer):
1) Initiate multipart upload of ~1.2M records via orchestrated chunker (chunks ~5MB).
2) Intentionally cancel the client process after chunk 3 (simulates a failed worker).
3) Client orchestration automatically resubmits remaining chunks using a new ephemeral API key within 10s.
4) Observe intermittent 429s across the next 3-10 minutes as load stabilizes.

Observed behavior: Support logs and rate-limiter traces show duplicate token debit events for some chunk uploads when the request path is retried with a new ephemeral key against the same route. The rate-window accounting shows a sawtooth refill pattern and temporary exhaustion of the tenant-level sustained bucket.

Expected behavior: Retries/resubmits should not cause double-counting across the same logical upload when the control plane marks the original upload cancelled; tenant accounting should prefer dedupe within the refill epoch for deduplicated preflight IDs.

Initial hypothesis: The orchestrator's quick key-churn combined with immediate resubmit is exposing a race between edge preflight dedupe and origin rate-window attribution. Cancelling at client side leaves partially-committed preflight metadata and the resubmit path is presenting a different credential, bypassing the preflight dedupe cache TTL.

Logs/metrics references:
- Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.company/d/ingest/tenant-429s?org=Datawave&from=now-2h&to=now
- Trace IDs (sample): 3f2a9c2b-2026-03-10T17:02Z, 8b1f4d5a-2026-03-10T17:07Z
- Rate-limiter debug excerpt: "tenant_token_debit: tenant=dw-233 count=120 epoch=161125 refill=60" repeated after a 10s gap

Notes: Customer is on enterprise SSO and rotates short-lived ephemeral keys for each orchestrator worker. They cannot trivially increase the resubmit backoff due to throughput SLAs.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Erin Patel (customer): We see the 429s only after we cancel jobs and the orchestrator replays with a fresh ephemeral key. If we avoid cancellation the job completes fine.

2026-03-10 - Support (Miguel Alvarez): Thanks Erin — capturing traces and rate-limiter counters. Can you share a packet capture or request IDs for one failing job? Also confirming which ephemeral key TTL your orchestrator uses.
2026-03-10 - Erin Patel (customer): We attached request IDs 3f2a9c2b, 8b1f4d5a in the original report. Key TTL is 30s; new keys issued on each worker start.

2026-03-11 - SRE (J. Huang): We reproduced a similar pattern in staging by simulating quick cancel+resubmit with different credentials. Observed duplicate preflight counts within same refill epoch. Filing a kernel-level race hypothesis to rate-limiter team.

2026-03-12 - Support (Miguel Alvarez): Temporary workaround validated with customer: increase ephemeral key TTL to 120s or add a 6s jitter on resubmit to avoid epoch alignment. Customer testing ongoing.
2026-03-12 - Customer (Erin): Increasing TTL to 120s significantly reduced 429 incidence in initial runs. We'll hold on production change until you confirm root cause and a permanent fix.

2026-03-12 - SRE (J. Huang): Next step: patch inbound preflight dedupe cache to key on logical upload id + tenant rather than credential id, and extend dedupe TTL for cancel-resubmit windows. Target PR created.
investigation_notes: Edge preflight cache TTL was 5s; customer resubmit happens within 10s — cache miss allowed duplicate preflight accounting.
Rate-limiter epoch alignment shows refill interval of 60s and tenant borrow disabled for dedicated pools by default.
Controlled staging test: cancel at chunk 3 and immediately resubmit with fresh credential -> tenant debit doubled for overlapping chunk IDs 3..7.
Correlation between key-churn and double-accounting stronger when ephemeral keys TTL < preflight TTL and resubmit jitter < 3s.
Related code area: ingest-orchestrator preflight tag generation (ingest-orchestrator/preflight.go) and edge preflight cache (edge/proxy/preflight_cache.go).
workaround: Customer-validated temporary mitigations: 1) increase ephemeral API key TTL to >=120s, 2) add 5-8s randomized jitter before resubmitting cancelled uploads, or 3) switch to reuse long-lived ingest key for orchestrator workers while we patch. All three reduce duplicate accounting symptoms.
resolution: Open — engineering patch in PR created to change preflight dedupe keying to (tenant, logical_upload_id) and extend cache TTL to 30s for dedicated pools. SRE will also add a telemetry tag to rate-limiter to detect future credential-churn double-debits. ETA for staging rollout: 2026-03-16. After rollout, we'll validate with Datawave on a mirrored job run.
next_steps: 1) Merge PR and roll to staging (engineers: @sre-team, @ingest-team). 2) Run controlled repro with Datawave mirrored job. 3) If validated, schedule production rollout with maintenance window and notify customer. 4) Postmortem/update runbook to document client resubmit patterns and recommended TTL/jitter guidance.
customer_impact_summary: Intermittent ingestion failures (429) for background bulk uploads when client cancels and immediately resubmits using short-lived keys. Workaround available; engineering fix targeting dedupe logic in preflight accounting.
